walkthrough_label: Example Patient C - emergency S2 (classic appendicitis)

presentation.summary: Hamza, 19, a student, is brought in by his brother at 10:00 with tummy pain since last night. Triage: abdominal pain 14 hours, HR 108, T 37.9, pain 8/10: very urgent.

history.answer: It started around my belly button around 8 last night, then moved down here [lower right] by the morning. I don't want to eat. I threw up once. Hurts when the car went over bumps.
No urine symptoms, no diarrhoea, no testicle pain.
No anaesthetic problems in the family.
Chicken and rice at 19:00 last night.

observations.note: Triage and first vital signs: only the heart rate is raised (91 to 110); NEWS2 1.
After analgesia and fluids: heart rate 96, pain 3/10.

examination.finding: Tender in the lower right tummy (McBurney's point), mild guarding, rebound tenderness medium, Rovsing's sign positive; the rest of the tummy is soft.

results.comment: First-responder cells high: suggests a bacterial cause
Not eating: starvation ketones; no infection or blood

problems.label: Severe pain (8/10) must not wait for the paperwork
problems.why: Analgesia does not hide the diagnosis; the clinician prescribes, the nurse gives.
expected_actions: Ask the nurse for pain relief now

problems.label: Probable appendicitis: scan, senior decision, antibiotics, theatre
problems.why: Story, examination, raised WBC and CRP and a positive ultrasound make simple appendicitis.
expected_actions: Pain relief, anti-sickness, IV fluids, nil by mouth
AIR 7 is indeterminate: request an ultrasound

problems.label: Emergency patient in pain with analgesia: treat as a full stomach
problems.why: Fasting times look adequate but the anaesthetist still plans a rapid sequence induction.

decisions.prompt: What do you do in the first 15 to 30 minutes?

options.text: Cannula and bloods, pain relief requested for the clinician to prescribe, anti-sickness if needed, IV fluids, nil by mouth, re-check vital signs
Wait for the scan result before any pain relief
options.consequence: Pain relief does not hide the diagnosis.
He may need surgery: nil by mouth.

decisions.prompt: AIR is 7 and AAS is 19. What now?

options.text: AIR 7 is indeterminate in this hospital's default score: request an ultrasound

decisions.prompt: The ultrasound shows a non-compressible 9 mm appendix with inflamed fat. What now?

options.text: Simple appendicitis: call the senior surgeon with SBAR; antibiotics now; anaesthetist review; consent; theatre promptly
options.consequence: Matches the book; timing per surgeon (WSES: within 24 hours of admission when surgery is indicated).

decisions.prompt: He is pain 3/10, alert and understands. How is consent handled?

options.text: Explain the diagnosis, laparoscopic removal, the risks and the alternative of antibiotics alone (CODA 29% needed surgery by 90 days; APPAC 39.1% recurrence in 5 years); teach-back; he chooses surgery and signs
Tell him he has no choice
options.consequence: Capacity and choice must be respected.

decisions.prompt: At Sign In: what is the aspiration risk?

options.text: YES: food at 19:00, strong painkillers, emergency: treat as a full stomach; RSI equipment and suction ready

options.consequence: Pain and opioids slow the stomach.

decisions.prompt: At Time Out (12:55): the antibiotic was given at 12:10. Is that in time?

options.text: Yes: given 45 minutes before, within the 60 minute rule; ultrasound displayed

correct: Quick identity check; allergies; ask the nurse for pain relief
Antibiotics; anaesthetic review; consent; handover; Sign In; Time Out at 12:55

incorrect.mistake: Makes him wait in pain while doing the paperwork
incorrect.risk: Suffering and a misleading heart rate
incorrect.recovery: Give pain relief and fluids, re-measure

incorrect.shows: A twisted testicle is missed in a young man

missed: Not giving antibiotics before Time Out
recovery: Give them and record the time; delay incision if under the 60 minute rule

debrief.why_priority: Pain relief does not wait; the diagnosis proceeds in parallel
debrief.related: Story, exam, bloods and scan fit together
debrief.independent: The ketones are starvation, not infection
debrief.trigger_escalation: NEWS2 7 or more, low BP or sepsis signs
debrief.remember: Treat the pain and think about the heart rate; do not assume a heart problem
